question: DeepGEMM #452 is a separate contiguous prefill MQA epilogue optimization, not the paged candidate-only decode patches. The live header still uses fmaxf and unhalved KV scales. Compare source-author H200 microbenchmarks against actual invocation/shape and exposed prefill time. The source claim that x+abs(x)=2relu(x) is exact for all finite float32 is too broad: finite x can overflow when doubled, and NaN behavior differs; require range/scaling/reference and top-k-set checks. H200 serving gain unmeasured. Prefer the smallest reversible JIT-header integration and a cold-prefill versus warm-cache discriminator. Extract short exact evidence, negative cases, distinction between contiguous and paged MQA, and deployment uncertainty. Do not treat a microbenchmark multiplier as serving improvement.

Summary
Replace
fmaxf(x, 0)
with
x + fabsf(x)
in the SM90 FP8 MQA logits epilogue, recovering the 2× throughput gap between FMNMX (half-rate) and FADD (full-rate) on Hopper. The factor-of-2 introduced by the identity is resolved by folding
0.5f
into the existing
scale_kv
multiply — zero extra instructions, bit-exact numerics.
Background
On SM90,
fmaxf(x, 0)
compiles to a single FMNMX, which issues at 64 ops/clk/SM — half the rate of FADD/FFMA (128 ops/clk/SM). Meanwhile
x + |x|
compiles to a single FADD with the absolute-value operand modifier, which is a free encoding bit in the instruction word:
FADD R3, R3, |R3|    ; one instruction, full rate (cuobjdump, sm_90a)
The relu executes once per
(token, head, kv)
score element in the MQA logits epilogue, so at 64 vs 128 ops/clk/SM the FMNMX form doubles the FP32 pipe time spent on relu alone.
Since
x + |x| = 2 · relu(x)
holds exactly for all finite IEEE-754 floats (
+0
for x ≤ 0), the doubled sum is simply halved by folding
* 0.5f
into the already-existing
scale_kv
multiplication (an exponent decrement, also exact):

sm100_mqa_logits.cuh

FADD2

The MR replaces
fmaxf(x, 0)
with
x + fabsf(x)
in the SM90 FP8 MQA logits epilogue (
sm90_fp8_mqa_logits.cuh
) and folds the compensating
* 0.5f

scale_kv

Verified points:
Numerics:
x + |x| == 2*relu(x)
is exact for all finite IEEE-754 floats (x>0: 2x; x<=0: exactly +0).
scale_kv * 0.5f
is an exact exponent decrement. Result is bit-identical to the previous path for finite accumulators.
Placement of the
0.5f
fold is correct: applied once per output element after the intra-thread reduction
(sum[0]+sum[1])
/
(sum[2]+sum[3])
and before the
__shfl_xor_sync
inter-thread reduction, so each of the
kNumHeads
contributing terms is halved exactly once.
scale_kv_0/1
are loop-invariant across the
BLOCK_Q
loop, so
scale_kv * 0.5f
is hoisted by nvcc — genuinely zero extra instructions per element.
NaN semantics:
fmaxf(NaN, 0)
returned 0, whereas
NaN + |NaN|
propagates NaN. This matches the SM100 kernel (
sm100_mqa_logits.cuh
L492-506 already uses the identical
x + |x|
trick via
__fadd2_rn
followed by
/ 2
), and WGMMA FP8 accumulators are finite in practice, so this is acceptable and consistent rather than new risk.
Scope: the paged MQA logits kernel is untouched, as stated.
No blocking issues. Performance claims (+3.7% avg, +7.4% on production shape, zero FMNMX in SASS) are plausible given FMNMX is half-rate on SM90 and the abs operand modifier is a free encoding bit on FADD; they were not re-measured here (no Hopper GPU in this environment). Two non-blocking, purely maintainability-oriented suggestions are left inline.
v4
Correct, low-risk SM90 micro-optimization. The MR replaces the half-rate
fmaxf(x, 0)
ReLU in the SM90 FP8 MQA logits epilogue with a full-rate FADD using the free absolute-value operand modifier (
x + |x|
), and compensates the resulting exact factor of 2 by folding
* 0.5f
into the already-present
scale_kv
multiply. I verified the change end to end: (1) for every finite IEEE-754 float,
x + |x| == 2*relu(x)
exactly (+0 for x <= 0, and
x + x == 2x
exactly for x > 0); (2) the factor-of-2 is uniform across the per-term weight multiply and across both the intra-thread and inter-thread (shuffle-xor) reductions, so it factors out exactly; (3)
scale_kv * 0.5f
is an exact power-of-two scaling for normal scales, so
fl((2*sum) * (scale/2)) == fl(sum * scale)
is bit-exact versus the previous
fmaxf
path. The change is local (3 lines in one file: line 286 transform plus the two
* 0.5f
folds at lines 297-298), preserves the kernel's dataflow/synchronization, and is consistent with the existing SM100
sm100_mqa_logits.cuh
implementation that already uses the same
fabsf
+
/2
identity. The claimed SASS result (a single FADD with the abs operand modifier replacing FMNMX) is consistent with the documented SM90 issue rates. Verified caveats, none blocking: (a) only non-finite inputs differ, since
fmaxf(NaN, 0) == 0
while
x + |x|
propagates NaN and
x == -inf
gives
NaN
; WGMMA accumulator outputs are finite in practice and this matches the SM100 kernel, so it is acceptable; (b) the exactness of the halving relies on
scale_kv
being normal (subnormal halving could lose a bit, and the doubled accumulator could overflow only near FLT_MAX), which realistic FP8 dequant scales and attention logits never approach. No correctness, safety, API, or concurrency issues found, and no changes requested.

claims.quote: Paged MQA logits (separate kernel, untouched) is unaffected.
claims.claim: Author-stated scope: #452 changes the contiguous SM90 FP8 MQA logits epilogue, separately from paged candidate-only decode optimizations.
claims.conditions: Execution must reach sm90_fp8_mqa_logits.cuh; the paged MQA kernel is outside this patch.
claims.reported_result: The author reports improvements for contiguous MQA and no effect on the separate paged kernel.
claims.transfer_inference: Attribute potential gains only to requests that execute the changed contiguous kernel. Do not transfer these measurements to paged decode.
claims.limitations: The supplied sources contain no target execution trace or candidate-only decode patch implementation. Runtime invocation frequency is unknown.

claims.claim: Observed source text: the installed contiguous epilogue retains fmaxf and multiplies the reduced sums directly by scale_kv_0 and scale_kv_1, without half-scale factors at those multiplication sites.
claims.conditions: Supplied read-only snapshot of the vendored SM90 contiguous MQA epilogue.
claims.reported_result: The visible epilogue does not contain #452's replacement or its two compensating half-scale factors.
claims.transfer_inference: This identifies a concrete patch candidate if the running process actually builds and invokes this header.
claims.limitations: Source inspection is not proof of the loaded implementation, generated instructions, invocation, or a measured bottleneck. Upstream scale definitions are outside the supplied code excerpt.

claims.quote: FADD R3, R3, |R3|    ; one instruction, full rate (cuobjdump, sm_90a)
claims.claim: Author claim: replacing FMNMX with FADD using its absolute-value operand modifier improves the instruction throughput of the ReLU operation.
claims.conditions: SM90A code generation; the author gives FMNMX and FADD rates of 64 and 128 operations per clock per SM, respectively.
claims.reported_result: The author reports zero FMNMX instructions across the tested JIT-instantiated contiguous MQA cubins and no additional instructions from scale compensation.
claims.transfer_inference: The mechanism is plausible when this epilogue consumes meaningful kernel time. Inspect generated code for the target's actual specializations.
claims.limitations: Disassembly files and target compiler details are not supplied. Doubling one instruction's issue rate does not double kernel or serving throughput.

claims.quote: Production indexer shapes, best of 3 reps, before → after:
claims.claim: Author-reported H200 microbenchmarks support a modest, shape-dependent contiguous-kernel improvement.
claims.reported_result: Respectively: 1018→1093 TFLOPS (+7.4%), 1042→1126 (+8.1%), 941→989 (+5.1%), and 980→1027 (+4.8%). The 192-case contiguous sweep reportedly averaged +3.7%, with SK=65536 averaging +4.4%, H=64 averaging +5.5%, and a best case of +11.3%.
claims.transfer_inference: Compare actual invocation shapes, head counts, dimensions, dtypes, and modes before choosing a representative microbenchmark. Larger SKV, more heads, and smaller head dimensions are author-proposed favorable conditions.
claims.limitations: Independent reproduction, timing distributions, uncertainty, worst-case results, and per-case regressions are unknown. D is unspecified for three listed cases, and CP is undefined in the excerpt. These are not serving measurements.

claims.quote: pass (numeric diff vs simulated reference, 20× bitwise self-consistency, mask equality)

claims.quote: holds exactly for all finite IEEE-754 floats
claims.claim: Analyst challenge: the universal exactness claim is too broad for this floating-point transformation with delayed compensation.
claims.conditions: Float32 addition, weighted products, reductions, and multiplication of the KV scale by 0.5.
claims.reported_result: The source claims exactness and bit-exact numerics, but supplies no overflow-boundary or subnormal-scale results.
claims.transfer_inference: A finite positive x such as FLT_MAX overflows when doubled under round-to-nearest float32 arithmetic. With unit weight and original scale 0.5, the original scalar contribution remains finite, while doubling x before applying the compensated scale 0.25 produces infinity. Weighted products and reductions also need overflow headroom; halving a subnormal scale can round or underflow. Require bounds and tests for accumulators, weights, scales, and intermediate reductions.
claims.limitations: This is an analytical counterexample, not an observed target failure. The target's numerical ranges, scaling constraints, rounding and flush-to-zero settings, and boundary-test outcomes are unknown. Finite accumulator inputs alone do not establish safety.
